name: Agency
use_label: Agent to-do cards for one person
one_liner: Turns work a coding agent finds into cards you decide with one click.

text.why: Putting an agent to work usually starts with you finding and writing down what to do. Agency reverses that: the agent looks through repositories, support tickets and messages for useful work, prepares fixes, replies and ideas as cards, and you only decide to send, apply or merge. It runs locally on Node.js as a single-user app; its routes are unauthenticated, so the README insists it stays on localhost. No license is stated in the README.
text.take: An attempt to take 'what should I ask it to do' off your plate, leaving only the decision.
build: An internal queue that turns support tickets into ready PRs and replies
A review desk where outreach drafts arrive as cards for a yes or no
An approval policy file rewritten to your team's rules

who.situation: running support, dev and outreach alone
too many small fixes to hand out one by one

start.text: Needs Node.js 22.13+ · open http://localhost:3100 in the browser
Unauthenticated single-user app: never expose via 0.0.0.0 or a tunnel

caveat: No license stated in the README
Unauthenticated routes: never expose it beyond localhost
The hero card is a fictional example, as the README notes

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: An Agency card: 'I fixed one customer issue.', a download-button before/after, and a 'Merge PR and message customer' button.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
